thread:
emily: hitting a weird one — customer reports JSON mode responses sometimes arrive as a malformed array after an auth retry. sample they captured: `[{\"id\":1,\"text\":\"ok\"}{\"id\":2,\"text\":\"ok2\"}]` (missing comma between objects).

jordan: do we have logs / seq numbers? which SDK + mode are they using?

emily: they say both Python and TS SDKs hit it. Go less frequent. Happens when token expires mid-stream and client does a refresh+retry. here's an anonymized extract from our logs:```
[INFO] 12:11:02 outbound request -> /v1/generate (stream)
[WARN] 12:11:07 401 Unauthorized (token expired)
[INFO] 12:11:07 token refresh start
[INFO] 12:11:08 token refreshed, retrying request on same connection
[INFO] 12:11:08 stream resumed, bytes recv: 1024
[DEBUG] 12:11:08 recv chunk: 0x5b 0x7b 0x22 0x69 0x64 ... 0x7d   <-- \"[{\"id\":1,...}]\" partial
[DEBUG] 12:11:08 recv chunk: 0x7b 0x22 0x69 0x64 ... 0x7d 0x5d  <-- \"{\"id\":2,...}]\" trailing
```

sandeep: my hunch: dechunker / frame boundary logic isn't being reset when the SDK does an auth retry on the same TCP/TLS connection, so two JSON object frames glue together without a comma. streaming JSONmode that emits arrays (not NDJSON) is sensitive to this.

jordan: can you paste a minimal repro we can run internally?

emily: minimal TS repro (pseudo):```ts
// client creates streaming request with auth callback
const res = await client.stream({model, input}, {onData: (chunk)=>parse(chunk)});
// auth callback refreshes token and triggers retry on same socket when 401 received
// server (test) simulates: sends partial array start + object, then closes chunk, then after retry sends next object without comma
```

emily: customer says workaround: disable connection reuse on retry (force new connection) and issue stops. they tested by setting `Connection: close` for the retry. :white_check_mark:

support-bot: escalated to eng-runtime + eng-ml for investigation (ticket #2467).

sandeep: proposed fix: when SDK performs an auth-retry that reuses the same stream, it should reset the streaming parser buffer (or treat retry as new stream). flushing the dechunk buffer on 401/retry event would prevent concatenating fragments. downside: could drop legitimately split token sequences if not handled carefully — need tests.

jordan: confirm this is JSON mode array-streaming (application/json stream where server streams objects within an array)?

emily: yes — specifically customers using \"JSON mode\" array-wrapped streaming output (not NDJSON).

sandeep: additional note: we should add e2e tests across py/ts/go SDKs that simulate mid-stream auth refresh and validate parser boundaries. i can draft test harness.

emily: attaching small curl-ish repro (manual):```
# client opens stream with token A
# server sends \"[{\"id\":1,\"t\":\"a\"}]\" then returns 401 during stream
# client refreshes token B and retries on same connection
# server resumes by sending \"{\"id\":2,\"t\":\"b\"}]\" -> results in ``[...}{...]`` glue
```

jordan: severity? customer impact? SLA?

emily: P2 for now, 1 enterprise customer blocked in prod for some endpoints, workaround requires connection close on retry. billing unaffected. ticket #2467 contains customer logs.

sandeep: assigning to eng-runtime, will draft a patch to flush parser state on retry + add tests. looping in @ingest-bot to run perf/regression on batching.

emily: thanks — keeping customer updated. will post any confirm + repro artifacts here. :rocket:
